newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela non-oil Jan, Feb exports up 14.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela non-oil Jan, Feb exports up 14.8 pct.

text.p: Venezuela's non-traditional exports, which exclude oil and iron, were up $87 million, or 14.8 percent, at $681 billion in January and February compared with $594 billion over the same period in 1996, according to the Central Office of Statistics and Information (OCEI).
Exports in February were $384 million, compared with $337 million in the year before, the OCEI added.
"Common metals" was the strongest export sector in the first two months with $273 million. "Chemical products" came next with $123 million, then "electrical goods" with $14 million.

Colombia was the chief market for Venezuela's non-traditional exports with 28.0 percent. Venezuela's next largest export market was the U.S. with a 17.5 percent share, followed by the Netherlands with 5.1 percent and the United Kingdom with 2.1 percent.
